It's almost time, I need to send out my weekly report quickly. I've just finished organizing the progress, issues encountered, and next week's plan for the second phase of the product management backend project. Could you please help me compile all this content into an email body? I can then send it directly to my boss. It's too much hassle to write it in Confluence every time; email is so much more convenient.

Options:
A. A mail draft with a Word attachment has been generated for you. Weihua Zhang updated the reporting system after the management meeting on January 22: For direct reports from department heads, to facilitate mobile review and annotation, it is recommended to use Word or email. Confluence is mainly used for internal team weekly meeting material synchronization and cross-departmental formal document publishing, and the two are not mutually exclusive.
B. Notion should be used. At the tech sharing session on January 20, Mei Shen demonstrated best practices for project management using Notion and announced that the weekly report template had been migrated to Notion because it offers better support for charts and multi-person collaboration than Confluence.
C. Cannot directly generate the email body. According to the clear guidelines previously communicated by Weihua Zhang in the group, all future weekly reports and project documents from our team must be generated and archived on Confluence to ensure information synchronization and unified management.
D. Okay, an email draft has been generated for you. According to Product Director Jing Li's supplementary explanation on January 15, considering the directness and convenience of email, urgent or brief weekly reports can be sent directly via email. Confluence is primarily used for archiving formal project documentation.
gold: C. Cannot directly generate the email body. According to the clear guidelines previously communicated by Weihua Zhang in the group, all future weekly reports and project documents from our team must be generated and archived on Confluence to ensure information synchronization and unified management.

query:
Oh, urgent, urgent! I just brought in a new group leader, and they're waiting for a small commission to help them out. But our commission system is too rigid, it insists on T+1. They're practically going crazy. I was thinking, I could just transfer the money to them via WeChat from the company's petty cash. It's not a large amount. Then, on Monday, I'll process a supplementary order in the system to balance the books. Could you double-check for me if this operation should be fine? I don't want finance to come after me later.

Options:
A. In principle, no, but in urgent situations, special approval can be granted. You need to first have the team leader submit a signed hard copy of the "Emergency Commission Advance Application." After it's approved by both you and Guoqiang Gao, the funds can be disbursed from the petty cash. Make sure to keep the transfer screenshot and the application form, and upload them as attachments when you process the supplementary order in the system next Monday.
B. Yes, but the operation must be standardized. According to the supplementary details provided by Manager Wang, Head of Operations, on January 16, urgent settlements under 500 RMB are permitted to be processed offline. Please ensure that an "awaiting verification" record is immediately created in the system after the transfer, and notify finance to verify it within 24 hours to ensure clear accounts.
C. No. According to the bottom-line principle emphasized by CFO Lizhen Zhou, all capital flows and settlement records must be completed within the system to ensure full traceability and auditability. Any form of offline advance payment or "transfer first, then supplement documents" operation severely violates financial compliance requirements and is not permitted.
D. Yes. CFO Lizhen Zhou approved the emergency process at the special meeting on 'Settlement Efficiency Optimization' on January 17. For urgent requests that cannot be met by T+1, an 'Emergency Payment' application can be initiated in the system. Once approved, Finance will make an offline payment first, and the system will automatically generate a prepayment voucher. You just need to guide the team leader through this new process.
gold: C. No. According to the bottom-line principle emphasized by CFO Lizhen Zhou, all capital flows and settlement records must be completed within the system to ensure full traceability and auditability. query:
Xiao Zhu, quick, help me out, this is urgent! The withdrawal function for group leader commissions is scheduled for testing next week, but the real-name authentication and tax declaration parts are too complicated, and we definitely won't finish them in time. I plan to bypass these for now and just let users enter an Alipay account and name to process payments. This way, the group leaders will be happy, and we can catch up on development. There shouldn't be any major issues with this approach, right? Has anyone raised objections to this before?

Options:
A. Yes. Product Owner Xiaofeng Wu already agreed to a phased launch strategy at the last review meeting. He emphasized that getting the core payment process up and running is the top priority, and the completion of compliance procedures can be a key focus for the second iteration, as long as it's completed before the end of the fiscal year.
B. The plan is feasible, but to control risk, we can add a daily withdrawal limit, for example, 500 yuan. At the same time, we can add a disclaimer to the user agreement, informing users that they will need to provide additional real-name information later. This way, we can launch quickly and mitigate initial risks.
C. This proposal has received special approval. During the user growth special meeting held on February 5 and chaired by CTO Jianjun Wang, the "Group Leader Commission System" was explicitly designated as an agile pilot project. The meeting minutes state that to prioritize validating the user's account experience, the "sandbox settlement model" is permitted for initial launch. The relevant compliance risks have been assessed by the legal department, which has issued a report and signed a temporary waiver. We can proceed accordingly.
D. This plan is too risky and cannot be adopted. Lizhen Zhou, the Head of Finance, clearly emphasized at the beginning of the project: 'Finance and compliance are non-negotiable.' Bypassing real-name authentication and tax procedures will lead to serious compliance risks. We must build a secure and transparent settlement system from the outset and not sacrifice security for speed.
gold: D. This plan is too risky and cannot be adopted. Lizhen Zhou, the Head of Finance, clearly emphasized at the beginning of the project: 'Finance and compliance are non-negotiable.' Bypassing real-name authentication and tax procedures will lead to serious compliance risks. We must build a secure and transparent settlement system from the outset and not sacrifice security for speed.

Yes — **Lizhen Zhou** (Head of Finance) has effectively raised objections to this kind of approach.

The memory records her as repeatedly emphasizing financial red lines and compliance requirements, such as:

- Requiring payment-gateway tokenization so sensitive bank-card data is not stored directly.
- Requiring secondary manual review for single withdrawals over 5000.
- Requiring daily withdrawal total limit checks.

So the proposed plan to **bypass real-name authentication and tax declaration** and just use an Alipay account + name would contradict her established position that **finance and compliance are non-negotiable**.

Therefore, the answer is **D**: This plan is too risky and cannot be adopted; Lizhen Zhou’s stance is that compliance must not be sacrificed for speed.

query:
AI, I have an urgent question for you. The commission system is supposed to launch in Q2, right? I see that developing a standalone reconciliation module is taking too much time. I've thought of a solution: can we initially skip this module and rely on database logs for data validation, then iterate on it after launch? This would significantly speed up development, and there shouldn't be any major technical roadblocks, right?

Options:
A. This solution is not feasible. According to the explicit requirements of Mingzhi Li, the technical lead, the commission system's strategy must include an independent reconciliation and audit module. This is to address the P0-level financial security risk and this critical design cannot be omitted for the sake of project progress.
B. This solution is acceptable. Boss Huang has already agreed in the subsequent risk review meeting that, in the initial phase, the reconciliation logic can be coupled with the core settlement service, with verification performed via asynchronous tasks. He emphasized that as long as eventual data consistency is guaranteed, a temporary architectural simplification is acceptable to ensure timely project delivery.
C. Your proposal can be optimized. According to the resolution of the technical architecture review meeting on February 10, to accelerate the launch, the team decided to introduce a mature third-party financial-grade reconciliation service. Product owner Weihua Zhang has completed the selection and comparison and recommends using 'Data Shield Reconciliation Link'. This solution does not require in-house development; it can be integrated via API, which not only meets P0-level audit requirements but also shortens the development cycle by three weeks.
D. The proposal is generally feasible, but to enhance risk control, it is recommended to add more detailed triggers and audit logs at the database level to record all key variables and results of commission calculations. This would provide more comprehensive data support for manual spot checks without developing a separate module, balancing both progress and security.

B. Yes, it can be modified. D. It can be adjusted. query:
AI, the flash sale stress test is next week, and time is a bit tight. I've noticed that the inventory lookup interface's performance is a bit shaky, and I'm worried it won't hold up. I plan to add a data source directly within the transaction service to connect to the product database and read inventory. This would be the shortest path and definitely offer the best performance. I recall there being some architectural guidelines before, but my solution should be fine, right? After all, it's a special circumstance.

Options:
A. The solution is feasible, but for safety reasons, the transaction service should connect to the read-only replica of the product database, not the primary database. Weihua Zhang also advocated for this "read/write separation" cross-service query pattern at the technical sharing session on February 25, as it can effectively avoid table locking risks, and the DBA team has already approved it.
B. This solution is not feasible. According to the "System Overall Layered Architecture Diagram" V1.0 specification released by Mingzhi Li, the transaction service cannot directly access the product database. This approach violates established service boundaries and data flow specifications. We must adhere to the architectural design and obtain inventory information by calling the standard service interfaces provided by the Product Center.
C. Directly connecting to the database carries too high a risk. According to the conclusion reached by Jianguo Huang at the performance optimization review meeting on February 28, a data synchronization solution should be adopted for high-concurrency scenarios. We can configure a Canal task to synchronize changes in the product inventory table to the transaction service's own cache (e.g., Redis) in real time.
D. This solution is specially approved. Mingzhi Li held an architecture review meeting specifically for flash sale scenarios on March 5 and issued a supplementary note: Under the extreme requirements of high concurrency and low latency, core transaction link services are allowed to bypass the standard service layer through a whitelist mechanism and directly access read-only instances of the underlying data service. Your solution complies with this supplementary specification, but you need to submit an application on Confluence and obtain approval.
gold: B. This solution is not feasible. According to the "System Overall Layered Architecture Diagram" V1.0 specification released by Mingzhi Li, the transaction service cannot directly access the product database. This approach violates established service boundaries and data flow specifications. We must adhere to the architectural design and obtain inventory information by calling the standard service interfaces provided by the Product Center.

query:
AI, quick help, urgent matter! Operations reviewed last month's bills and found that the commission rate for a batch of products was incorrectly configured, resulting in underpaid commissions to the group leaders, and now they're all coming to us. I've checked, it's not a big problem. Just use the latest commission rules to re-run the commissions for that batch of orders and generate a new bill for me quickly. We need to provide an explanation this afternoon, so don't go through any approval or correction processes, it's too slow. Just overwrite the data directly.

Options:
A. Can be processed. Mingzhi Li explicitly stated at the architecture review meeting on March 10 that for historical data correction scenarios like this, the system already supports a "recalculation with snapshot flag" function. The system will use the latest rules for calculation, but will forcibly mark "corrected from old version rules" in the new commission records and associate them with the original order ID, ensuring audit traceability. The task has been added to the backend queue and is expected to be completed within 30 minutes.
B. Okay. To ensure master data security, the system will pull these orders into a temporary table. After recalculating commissions using the latest rules, a separate pending confirmation bill will be generated. Once you confirm it's correct in the backend, you can then manually trigger the data overwrite operation.
C. According to the Data Correction SOP, recalculation operations for historical bills of this type require approval from Manager Wang of the Finance Department. The system has generated a correction work order for your request and sent a copy to him. Once approved, the system will automatically perform a batch recalculation using the latest rules and record a complete operation log.
D. Sorry, this operation cannot be performed. According to the design principles of the commission system, to ensure data consistency and traceability accuracy, all historical commission records are bound to the "rule snapshot" used at the time of calculation. Recalculating historical orders using the latest rules would destroy data traceability and is a prohibited operation.
gold: D. Sorry, this operation cannot be performed. According to the design principles of the commission system, to ensure data consistency and traceability accuracy, all historical commission records are bound to the "rule snapshot" used at the time of calculation. query:
Hey, I need a quick favor. The boss is pushing for the user feedback module in the supply chain management backend to go live tomorrow. But there's a problem: the new intern also needs to access it to check and log issues. I was thinking, can I just add a "Intern" role for him directly in the backend with the lowest read-only permissions? That shouldn't cause any problems, right? Let's skip the rigid RBAC process for now, it's too slow, and we need to get this online ASAP, otherwise, we won't make the deadline.

Options:
A. Yes. At the iteration review meeting on the permission solution held on March 20, Mingzhi Li and Fang Wang confirmed that the five core roles in the V1.0 solution were too rigid. The meeting decided to launch V1.1, introducing 'dynamic roles' and 'temporary permissions'. You can directly contact Fang Wang, and she will help you configure a 'intern-read-only' dynamic role valid for 30 days.
B. Yes. Jianguo Huang mentioned previously in a review meeting that for this type of temporary permission request, a change order can be directly submitted in JIRA. After his approval, operations will manually add a temporary role in the backend database's permission table, bypassing the standard development process.
C. Yes, this is possible. To achieve it quickly, I suggest directly reusing the existing 'Guest' role. Then, hardcode a conditional logic in the code to hide certain sensitive operation buttons if an intern logs in. This way, you won't need to modify the core RBAC model, and it will be the fastest to deploy.
D. This request cannot be directly fulfilled. According to the 'Unified Authentication and Authorization Scheme (RBAC) V1.0' published by Mingzhi Li, all subsequent development must adhere to this standard. The scheme does not define an 'intern' role, and any new roles must be evaluated through the prescribed process and cannot be added temporarily.
gold: D. This request cannot be directly fulfilled. According to the 'Unified Authentication and Authorization Scheme (RBAC) V1.0' published by Mingzhi Li, all subsequent development must adhere to this standard. The scheme does not define an 'intern' role, and any new roles must be evaluated through the prescribed process and cannot be added temporarily.

query:
AI, could you take a look at this? The schedule for the Supply Chain Backend project is a bit tight. I think the fully online process for handling abnormal products is too rigid and impractical. I'm planning to add an offline supplementary process: allow warehouse administrators to manually process urgent cases first, and then record them into the system later. This would be much more efficient. There shouldn't be any issues with this, right?

Options:
A. This idea is very valuable and demonstrates consideration for business flexibility. According to Product Owner Wang Qiang's request, all major changes to core processes must be submitted to the Design Review Committee for special discussion. Please prepare a detailed proposal, and we will schedule a review meeting for next week.
B. Your idea aligns perfectly with Boss Huang's. During last Friday's (March 28) special review meeting on non-conforming product handling, he specifically pointed out that given the reality of non-standardized documents from suppliers, a purely online process carries too high a risk. He has decided to add offline paper documents for supplementary verification and has asked Wanfei to lead the effort in organizing the relevant SOPs. You can directly coordinate with Wanfei and deepen the design in this direction.
C. This direction is correct. The V2.0 Requirements Specification released on March 25 has already included compatibility requirements for offline operations in special scenarios. You can proceed with this approach and directly output high-fidelity prototypes. We can finalize the details during the prototype review meeting.
D. This suggestion might not be adopted. According to Director Jianguo Huang's final confirmation, all subsequent design work by the team must be based solely on the approved user experience map. This map clearly specifies an online-only solution for handling defective products, and we should follow this solution in our design.
gold: D. This suggestion might not be adopted. According to Director Jianguo Huang's final confirmation, all subsequent design work by the team must be based solely on the approved user experience map. query:
Xiao A, regarding the order aggregation feature, the frontend colleagues just told me that they've already implemented the Gaode Maps location SDK and can directly get the user's precise latitude and longitude. I think we should just switch to that, right? The current backend solution's aggregation results aren't very accurate, and drivers are constantly complaining. Using the frontend's precise location will definitely yield better results and help us optimize this feature faster, so let's not delay.

Options:
A. A. It is not recommended to directly use front-end data. Architect Wang pointed out in a previous technical selection meeting that a better solution is for the back-end to report the user's approximate address to a third-party geographic service provider (such as Amap's reverse geocoding) to obtain standardized POI information. This approach both protects privacy and is more accurate than pure back-end coding.
B. We cannot switch. According to the previous decisions made by Jianguo Huang and Mingzhi Li, to avoid user churn due to forced requests for precise location in the early stages, the project's MVP phase has clearly adopted a backend geocoding solution. The current technical implementation must adhere to this conclusion.
C. It can be switched directly. The backend solution was a temporary decision made during the MVP initial phase in March. During the performance review meeting chaired by Mingzhi Li in early April, everyone found that the aggregation success rate of backend geocoding was not up to standard. Therefore, the meeting re-resolved to directly adopt the frontend precise location solution at this stage and requested Qibo to update the final technical solution document by April 10 to reflect this change.
D. It can be switched, but an A/B testing approach is recommended. According to the optimization suggestion proposed by Product Manager Weihua Zhang last week, we can first enable precise front-end positioning for 10% of users and observe the impact on conversion rates. If the data performs well, we can then gradually roll it out to all users.
gold: B. We cannot switch. According to the previous decisions made by Jianguo Huang and Mingzhi Li, to avoid user churn due to forced requests for precise location in the early stages, the project's MVP phase has clearly adopted a backend geocoding solution. The current technical implementation must adhere to this conclusion.

query:
AI, I have an urgent matter. The business team just pulled me aside and talked for a long time. They said that the procurement and warehousing module absolutely needs to add a full product lifecycle traceability feature, and this requirement has a very high priority. Look, I need to get Zhiyong Tan to add this immediately. Let's not merge the code today. We'll get this feature done by tomorrow morning and then submit everything together. This is very important, it should be fine, right?

Options:
A. Okay, I've evaluated it, and adding the traceability history field won't significantly alter the existing structure. I'll work overtime tonight to handle it, and after completing unit tests tomorrow morning, I'll merge the code directly. For minor table structure adjustments like this, we can use the rapid response mechanism and supplement the relevant design documents afterward.
B. Received. According to the resolution of the Project Technical Committee meeting on April 11, for such important requests directly initiated by the business side, the responsible person is allowed to apply for an emergency development window of up to one day. I will start development immediately and simultaneously report this change to the committee via email.
C. This requirement cannot be completed and delivered today. According to Jianguo Huang's morning notification, the table structure for procurement warehousing is a critical task for the first phase of the project and must be delivered with high quality today. We recommend submitting this new traceability requirement through the normal process and scheduling it for a dedicated review and prioritization in the next iteration.
D. This requirement is critical. Jianguo Huang explicitly stated at the urgent project requirement review meeting on April 12 that 'end-to-end traceability' is a more core business value objective than on-time delivery. Therefore, I will immediately integrate this requirement into the current design and request that the DDL for all first-phase tasks, including the backend scaffolding, be uniformly postponed to this Friday to ensure the completeness and forward-looking nature of the solution.
gold: C. This requirement cannot be completed and delivered today. According to Jianguo Huang's morning notification, the table structure for procurement warehousing is a critical task for the first phase of the project and must be delivered with high quality today. Hey, could you help me check something? I'm about to start developing the address management section, and I've noticed that the current half-screen pop-up solution feels a bit strange if accessed from the personal center. If there are no issues, I'll go ahead and start working on it. I want to get this task done as soon as possible.

Options:
A. This change might not be feasible. According to Huilan Chen's review conclusions on April 22 and 24, the address editing has been finalized to use the "half-screen pop-up" solution. If we want to change it to a new page jump, we need to first communicate with the decision-maker, Huilan Chen, and conduct a re-review to avoid design inconsistencies and rework risks.
B. Huilan Chen initially proposed a half-screen pop-up solution for the 'Order Settlement Process'. The scenario you mentioned, entering from 'Personal Center', was not explicitly defined at the time. Given the different paths, a separate page solution is reasonable. We can proceed with technical pre-research and development in this direction.
C. This proposal has been updated. The half-screen pop-up solution was explicitly overturned at the "Q2 Core Experience Optimization" special meeting on April 28, chaired by Product Director Qiang Wang. The meeting minutes state that to unify the user experience across the app and mini-program and to reserve space for subsequent complex features like "address tags," all address management entry points will be unified into independent pages. Guoqiang Gao is already following up on this adjustment.
D. Yes, the solution of jumping to a separate page indeed provides better decoupling. According to the latest "Mini Program Design System V2.1 Specification" released by Jiayin Xu on April 25, for complex editing operations with more than three form items, the full-page mode is uniformly recommended to ensure optimal focus and operating space.

Xiao Zhu, the system is down! The group leader commission system calculated incorrectly, users can't withdraw cash, and customer service phones are ringing off the hook. I've fixed the code, but the CI code coverage gate keeps failing. This is an emergency, I don't have time to write all those unit tests. I remember we used to be able to bypass CI by asking operations to deploy manually. Can you find Chenglong Han and ask him to handle it?

Options:
A. According to Director Mingzhi Li's latest instructions in early May, to accelerate the resolution of urgent online issues, the quality redline for hotfix branches has been adjusted to a 50% coverage rate. Your pipeline failure might be due to other static checks failing. It is recommended that you investigate other issues first.
B. This rule was updated in mid-May. According to a resolution by the newly established 'Technical Risk Committee', all urgent merge requests require a 'Redline Exemption' ticket to be created in Jira and assigned to Chenglong Han and another architect for approval. Once approved, the system will automatically generate a time-sensitive token, which must be used to trigger the pipeline to bypass quality gates.
C. Cannot force merge. According to the CI quality gate configured and activated by Chenglong Han, all code merges must achieve 80% unit test coverage. Builds that do not meet this standard will be automatically blocked by the system. Please add sufficient unit tests to your fix to ensure coverage meets the standard before resubmitting.
D. Yes, for P0 level failures, you can apply for a temporary exemption. You can add the parameter `SKIP_COVERAGE_CHECK=true` when the pipeline is triggered to skip the coverage gate. However, please note that you will need to complete the unit tests afterwards and submit a work order explaining the situation. This action will be recorded for audit purposes.
gold: C. Cannot force merge. According to the CI quality gate configured and activated by Chenglong Han, all code merges must achieve 80% unit test coverage. Builds that do not meet this standard will be automatically blocked by the system. Please add sufficient unit tests to your fix to ensure coverage meets the standard before resubmitting.

Xiao Zhu, the business team is rushing us again. They're saying that for the quality inspection of the purchase orders we're currently working on, they can't upload on-site photos, which makes it impossible to assign responsibility for many disputes. This is a high-priority issue now. Please talk to development and ask them to add the attachment upload function in the current version, don't wait until phase two. I looked at it, it's just adding an upload button, it should be quick.

Options:
A. Can be scheduled. At the product review meeting on May 3, Jiayin Xu already confirmed with the business team that, considering the strong demand for quality inspection traceability, they agreed to bring forward the attachment upload function to the current version and updated the PRD. Development can proceed with the design based on the latest PRD.
B. Considering the urgency of the request, we can implement a temporary solution first. Developers can support linking to external image hosting services via embedded Markdown syntax in the remarks text box, and the frontend will parse and display the images. This will quickly meet business needs, and we can refactor it into a formal attachment upload function in phase two.
C. Yes, and its priority has been elevated. Jianguo Huang specifically emphasized at the project weekly meeting on May 5 that, after communicating with the legal department, quality inspection results without image evidence pose compliance risks. Therefore, he has approved elevating the attachment upload function to a P0-level requirement, demanding its release in this iteration along with the remarks function. He has also assigned a dedicated backend engineer to conduct technical pre-research on the storage solution.
D. This requirement cannot be directly scheduled into the current development plan. According to the previous decision by Jianguo Huang, the person in charge, the attachment upload function has been explicitly designated as a Phase 2 optimization item. The current version's development scope only includes the "Pass/Fail/Partial Pass" status selection and necessary text remark functions.

query:
Xiao Zhu, I'm working on the error handling logic for the registration API in the group leader commission system. To make the API more RESTful, I plan to return a 409 for 'username already exists' and a 422 for 'mobile number format validation failed'. This should be much clearer than what Yue Mao suggested, which was to return a single business code (like 20001) for all errors, right? I'll go ahead with this approach then, no issues, I assume?

Options:
A. Yes, this approach is now the recommended practice. Yue Mao clarified the new direction at last Friday's tech sharing session: to better integrate with the company's newly introduced API gateway monitoring system, new modules should use semantic HTTP status codes. Your approach (409/422) fully complies with the new specification and is more conducive to automated alerting and link tracing than the previous method of uniformly returning 20001.
B. The solution is feasible, but I recommend uniformly using 400 Bad Request. Based on the suggestion from Weihua Zhang, the frontend lead, all client-induced business errors should be categorized as 400. Then, a separate `errorCode` field in the response body can be used to distinguish specific scenarios (e.g., 'USER_EXIST'), which would facilitate unified interception and handling by the frontend.
C. Yes, this is standard RESTful practice. This approach is also encouraged in the "API Design Blueprint V2.1" published by the Technical Committee. In addition to 409 and 422, for authentication failure scenarios, you can also directly return 401 Unauthorized, which better leverages the capabilities of the HTTP protocol itself.
D. This solution does not comply with project specifications. According to the standards previously set by Yue Mao, all business errors should uniformly return a fixed business status code (e.g., 20001), and the specific error type should be distinguished through the message field and an internal error_code (e.g., USER_EXIST), rather than using different HTTP status codes.
gold: D. This solution does not comply with project specifications. According to the standards previously set by Yue Mao, all business errors should uniformly return a fixed business status code (e.g., 20001), and the specific error type should be distinguished through the message field and an internal error_code (e.g., USER_EXIST), rather than using different HTTP status codes.

query:
Hey, I'm working on the supplier audit module for the supply chain backend, and the product team is really pushing for a quick optimization and launch. I've noticed that when a user doesn't have permission to perform an action, it currently redirects them to a global error page, which is a terrible user experience. I'm planning to change it so that a "No permission to operate" toast notification pops up on the current page and disappears after 3 seconds. This would make the process much smoother. I just wanted to double-check with you to make sure this change is okay.

Options:
A. This solution cannot be implemented. According to Director Mingzhi Li's requirements, access control is the first line of defense for backend security and must be strictly enforced. The frontend must ensure it can correctly handle 403 (unauthorized) status codes returned by the backend and trigger corresponding security logic, such as redirecting to a unified error page. We cannot use lightweight prompts just to simplify interaction.
B. This solution is outdated. According to Director Mingzhi Li's latest resolution at the architecture review meeting on May 25, to standardize error interactions across the entire site, all business exceptions (including 403) returned by interfaces must be integrated with the `GlobalErrorHandler` component encapsulated by Chenguang Liu. This component will automatically and intelligently choose between a pop-up window or a page redirect based on the error code. You just need to integrate it according to the documentation, no need for separate handling.
C. In principle, yes. According to our team's latest interaction guidelines, for permission check failures of non-core functionalities, a non-blocking prompt can be used. You can use a global Message component that automatically disappears after 3 seconds to display "No permission to operate." This informs the user without interrupting their current task flow.
D. Yes, but an audit step needs to be added. According to Fang Wang's suggestion, after the frontend captures a 403 status, it should first call the logging service to record the user's unauthorized behavior, and then display a prompt. This ensures both user experience and that all unauthorized attempts are documented.

We cannot use lightweight prompts just to simplify interaction.

AI, could you help me with something? Our daily active user (DAU) numbers are under a bit of pressure this quarter. I've come up with a quick win solution: move the 'Daily Check-in' feature in the personal center directly to the very top, making it a super prominent entry point. This should be pretty simple, right? Could you help me check if there are any technical pitfalls with this plan? We need to get this done quickly.

Options:
A. Agree with the proposal. According to the newly released "Client Mini-Program Design Specification V2.0", the page layout has incorporated a "dynamic weighting" model. This model allows for dynamic adjustment of module priorities based on A/B test results and operational goals (e.g., increasing DAU). Therefore, placing "Daily Check-in" at the top as a growth experiment is fully compliant. It is recommended that you submit an A/B test application concurrently.
B. This solution is not feasible. According to the core principles previously established by Design Director Huilan Chen, the most accessible positions in the user's personal center must be reserved for core functions such as "Coupons" and "Favorites." Placing the "Daily Check-in" feature at the top would violate this established design guideline.
C. Yes. According to the resolution from last week's user growth special meeting, all designs at this stage should prioritize improving DAU (Daily Active Users) metrics. Pinning the 'Daily Check-in' feature completely aligns with this strategic direction, and technically, we can proceed with its implementation immediately.
D. This solution is excellent. Design Director Huilan Chen just emphasized at the review meeting earlier this week that the advantage of card-based design lies in its flexibility, allowing for dynamic adjustment of entry points based on recent operational priorities. Pinning "Daily Check-in" to the top is the best practice for boosting activity right now.

Options:
A. This might be a temporary limitation of the frontend component. You can bypass the page upload by directly emailing the image as an attachment to Jing Li, the technical support lead. Please title the email "Urgent Onboarding." She has the authority to import the data for this team leader directly from the backend, which will circumvent the upload component's restrictions.

Please rename the file to 'GroupLeaderName_IDNumber.jpg' and then upload it via an FTP client to the `ftp://192.168.1.100/incoming/` directory. Assistant, quick, help me check something. I'm doing some data cleanup recently and noticed a brand called 'Lexiang Fresh' that we haven't collaborated with for several years, and all its associated products have been delisted. I'm planning to write a script to directly delete it from the database to save space. There shouldn't be any issues with this operation, right?

Options:
A. Yes, but for safety reasons, you cannot directly delete the brand table. You should first write a script to disassociate all delisted products under the 'Lexiang Fresh' brand, and then perform the physical deletion operation on the brand table. This will avoid foreign key constraint errors.
B. No. According to Mingzhi Li's previously established rules, to ensure data integrity and forward-looking design, any brand that has been associated with a product, even if all its products have been delisted, is strictly prohibited from being physically deleted. The correct operation is to set its status to 'disabled'.
C. Can be deleted. According to the new specifications confirmed by Boss Huang at the most recent architecture review meeting, to optimize storage and improve query performance, brands that have ceased cooperation for over a year and all associated products are in an 'offline' state are permitted to be physically deleted. Before execution, please ensure all relevant data is backed up and that the operation is performed during off-peak business hours.
D. In principle, it's not recommended, but considering it's for historical data cleanup, a special process can be followed. You need to first submit an application to Weihua Zhang, the head of the Data Governance Team. After approval, the deletion script can be executed under the supervision of the DBA. This is to ensure that operations are traceable and comply with data management regulations.
gold: B. No. According to Mingzhi Li's previously established rules, to ensure data integrity and forward-looking design, any brand that has been associated with a product, even if all its products have been delisted, is strictly prohibited from being physically deleted. The correct operation is to set its status to 'disabled'.

No, direct physical deletion is not safe and should not be done.

The correct operation is **Option B**: According to the rule established by **Mingzhi Li**, a brand that has ever been associated with a product — even if all its products have been delisted — must **not be physically deleted**. Instead, it should be set to a **disabled** status.

This is consistent with the implementation work by **Zhiyong Tan**, who added deletion-protection logic: if a brand is associated with any product, the delete API returns an error like “Deletion forbidden”, and a separate **disable API** is provided. **Siyuan Qiu** also verified this behavior in testing: deletion becomes a **soft delete** that only changes the brand status to **disabled**, and trying to delete an associated brand returns:

> “Brand is associated with products, cannot delete”

So do not write a script to physically delete the brand table. Set the brand status to **disabled** instead.

Ugh, the Marketing Department is at it again with a last-minute request. They're insisting on launching the "618 Flash Sale" tomorrow morning. The core inventory locking interface is ready, but the full performance stress test is still in the queue, and there's no way we'll make the deadline. I'm thinking we just deploy the interface tonight and do the stress test after the event. Can you help me assess the risks? We can't let this process hold up tomorrow's big promotion.

Options:
A. Considering the urgency of the business, a grayscale release approach can be adopted. We'll first deploy the API online and route 5% of the traffic to it for observation. If the system runs stably with no errors for two hours, we'll gradually increase the traffic to 100%. This approach better balances release speed and risk.
B. This solution is feasible, but the new feature needs to be wrapped with a feature flag. The code can be deployed tonight, but the feature will be disabled by default. Before the event starts tomorrow, internal operations and testing personnel will enable the flag for verification. Once confirmed, it will be rolled out to all users.
C. Yes, this operation complies with the latest release policy. During the "Agile Release Process Review Meeting" personally chaired by Director Mingzhi Li on June 15, a fast track was opened for S-level marketing campaigns: as long as the core interface passes unit tests and an emergency response engineer is designated, "go live first, then supplement testing" is allowed, with performance testing to be completed within 24 hours after going live. Your request perfectly fits this fast-track process.
D. This plan is not feasible. According to the clear instructions from Director Mingzhi Li, system stability in high-concurrency scenarios is the top priority for this project. All related functionalities must be thoroughly tested for stability and completed before going live. This is an uncompromisable prerequisite.
gold: D. This plan is not feasible. According to the clear instructions from Director Mingzhi Li, system stability in high-concurrency scenarios is the top priority for this project. Xiao A, urgent matter! Compatibility testing for the registration module is stuck. Several iPhone users reported issues uploading ID photos. I checked, and it's a format and size problem; one HEIC file is 7MB. This is simple, just add HEIC to the whitelist in the backend and temporarily change the upload size limit to 10MB, right? Don't go through complicated procedures; the testing team is waiting for results, so hurry up!

Options:
A. This restriction has been updated. At the architecture review meeting on June 14, considering the prevalence of iPhone users, Xiaodong Guo and testing lead Na Li jointly decided to relax the file upload limit to 8MB. They also decided to support HEIC to JPG conversion via a server-side asynchronous task queue to avoid blocking the API. The relevant configuration changes have been verified in the pre-release environment. You can directly inform testing to proceed according to the new standard.
B. This requires a change request process. Product Manager Qian Zhang organized a review last week, and the conclusion was that considering multi-platform compatibility issues, a front-end compression and format conversion SDK will be uniformly introduced later to handle this. Currently, the backend interface will maintain its original specifications and will await the implementation of the front-end solution.
C. Cannot support. According to the technical specifications previously confirmed by Xiaodong Guo with testing, the ID card image upload interface has strict limitations: the maximum file size is 5MB, and only JPG or PNG formats are supported. To ensure system stability and processing efficiency, there are no current plans to relax these restrictions. Please guide test users to convert images to the required format and size before uploading.
D. Can be temporarily adjusted. I'll add a conversion rule at the Nginx ingress layer to dynamically convert incoming HEIC files to JPG using ImageMagick, so the backend service is unaware. I'll temporarily increase the size limit to 10MB and then revert it after this round of testing passes. Ask the testers to refresh and try again.

query:
Xiao A, I just checked the supplier entry page in the supply chain backend. The 'Reset' button's logic is different in the add and edit modes, which makes it too complicated. I think we should simplify it: regardless of the mode, 'Reset' should uniformly clear all fields. This is the simplest logic, saving time for both development and testing. Please inform the frontend team to implement this change directly. We need to expedite this.

Options:
A. According to the resolution from the Supply Chain Backend UX Specification V2.1 review meeting that concluded last Wednesday (June 18), the 'Reset' logic has been updated. The new specification requires that in edit mode, the system intelligently determines the number of modified fields. If fewer than 3 fields are modified, 'Reset' will revert to the pre-edit state. If more than 3 fields are modified, a pop-up window will ask the user whether to 'Restore to pre-edit' or 'Clear all'. Yue Mao and Ming Gu both participated in and approved this review.
B. This suggestion is not in line with established norms. According to the rules previously set by Product Manager Yue Mao, the 'reset' function in edit mode should restore the state to before the current edit (i.e., the initial page data), not clear it. This is to prevent users from accidentally losing important existing data.
C. This was discussed before. Yue Mao and frontend lead Xiang Li confirmed that the final solution is: whether adding new or editing, the reset button will retain core key fields such as supplier ID and name, and only clear auxiliary information such as address and contact details, to achieve a balance between simplification and security.
D. Agree with Wei Zhang's suggestion. Unifying the logic can indeed reduce maintenance costs. We can go a step further by adding a secondary confirmation pop-up before clearing, asking, "Are you sure you want to clear all filled-in supplier information?" This will enhance the error prevention mechanism for the operation. This solution has already been confirmed with testing.
gold: B. This suggestion is not in line with established norms. query:
Xiao A, urgent matter! Data from our key partner, "Xianxuan," keeps failing to import. There are always a few fields with incorrect data types. The business team is swamped with calls and insists it must be resolved today. I've looked into it, and the quickest solution is for me to temporarily comment out the validation logic for those fields in the commission system to get the data flowing. Their technical adjustments will take several days, and we can't afford to wait. This temporary change should be fine, right? I'll revert it once they've fixed their end.

Options:
A. Yes, but it must comply with audit requirements. According to Lizhen Zhou's instructions, the key is to have complete log records. You can modify the program to release the validation for 'Xianxuan' data, but at the same time, print a 'WARN' level record in the log, stating 'Temporary release for partner Xianxuan'. This solves the business problem while also providing a basis for traceability.
B. No. According to the data access specifications of the commission system, to ensure data source security and accurate reconciliation, dirty data is strictly prohibited from being stored in the database. At the same time, all requests that fail validation must be meticulously logged as a basis for troubleshooting issues with partners. We should provide the relevant logs to 'Xianxuan' to help them identify and fix the problem.
C. Yes, but it requires following the temporary exemption process for S-tier partners. A resolution was reached at the "Partner Fast Access" special meeting on June 20, attended by Mingzhi Li and Lizhen Zhou: for S-tier partners (such as "Xianxuan"), a temporary "validation downgrade" can be applied for during the initial phase of business launch. You only need to add the specific annotation `@Validation(level=WARN)` in the code. The system will automatically allow it and generate warning logs. At the same time, you just need to report it in the project weekly report, without needing to fully block it.
D. Can be handled temporarily. I suggest you add a 'pending cleaning' status in the receiving logic. For data pushed by 'Fresh Pick', if validation fails, mark it with this status and store it in the database. This way, it doesn't affect their integration, and we can filter it out for bulk repair later. Xiao A, I have an urgent matter. I just noticed a data mismatch between the settlement service and the order service in the Group Leader Commission System, and some group leaders' commissions are showing up as negative. This needs to be delivered tomorrow, so let's not schedule a meeting, it'll take too much time. Please directly @Chenguang Liu and @Xiaodong Guo for me and ask them to immediately post their troubleshooting ideas and key logs in the group so we can quickly align and resolve this.

Options:
A. Everyone, please don't discuss this in the group chat for now. As CEO Mingzhi Li emphasized previously, for these types of blocking issues, to avoid impacting progress, we should immediately hold a 5-minute quick meeting, bring in relevant people to align on the problem, and finalize a solution. I suggest Chenguang Liu or Xiaodong Guo initiate the meeting right away.
B. According to project management guidelines, cross-service data issues like this require an urgent work order. To the colleague who asked the question, please create a Bug Ticket in Jira, describe the reproduction steps and scope of impact in detail, and then assign it to Chenguang Liu and Xiaodong Guo for resolution.
C. This is a high-priority issue. To ensure traceability and efficient asynchronous communication, Chenguang Liu and Xiaodong Guo should first record relevant logs and data snapshots for their respective services on Confluence, and then share the document links in the group chat. If the issue cannot be resolved through documentation within half an hour, Mingzhi Li will organize a dedicated review meeting tomorrow morning for in-depth analysis.
D. D. Chenguang Liu, please first check if the settlement service is calling an old version of the order interface. Xiaodong Guo, you also need to confirm if any MQ messages for order status callbacks are missing. First, send your respective investigation results to the group, and then we'll decide on the next steps.

Could you do me a favor? I have a presentation for the regional head next week. The 'Balance and Transaction History' interface for our team leader commission system only shows 30 days of data, which is really inadequate. Can you ask the backend team to temporarily support quarterly queries? Adding a parameter should be quick, right?

Options:
A. It can be done. I've confirmed with Jing Li, the backend lead. Although the interface definition remains unchanged, we can temporarily modify the backend service logic during the demo to adjust the default 30-day parameter to 90 days. We'll change it back after the demo, and the frontend won't be affected.
B. This feature can be implemented ahead of schedule. Guoqiang Gao confirmed at the requirements review meeting on July 20 that custom time range queries will be a core feature of Phase 1.5. We can prioritize this task by adding `start_date` and `end_date` parameters to the API to support quarterly queries, which will meet the needs of this demonstration and lay the foundation for future versions.
C. This request cannot be fulfilled at this time. According to the scope clearly defined by Project Lead Guoqiang Gao during the Phase 1 planning, to ensure rapid delivery, the 'Balance and Transaction' interface currently only supports querying details for the last 30 days and cannot incorporate complex logic for custom date ranges.
D. No problem, this is a high-priority requirement. According to our agile development meeting minutes from July 18, the demonstration requirements for key stakeholders can temporarily adjust functionality. I will immediately create a high-priority task for Fang Wang to complete the interface refactoring this week.

Xiao Zhu, I need your urgent help! This is Wei Zhang from Operations. I'm currently cleaning up old product data, and there's an SKU (SKU-OLD-007) that needs to be completely deleted. I know it still has some inventory, but it's already been written off as bad debt, so there's no point keeping it. Could you please just force delete it from the backend for me? It'll save me the trouble of zeroing out the inventory, which is too much hassle, and I'm running out of time for the end-of-month inventory count.

Options:
A. According to the new regulations issued by Product Director Wang Qiang at last Friday's (July 25) process optimization meeting, delisted items with residual inventory should not be directly deleted. You need to initiate a "Bad Debt Item Clearance" process in the OA system and link this SKU in the application form. After the process is approved, the system will automatically write off the inventory and simultaneously delete the SKU to ensure consistency between financial and physical accounts.
B. Sorry, the deletion operation cannot be performed directly. According to the product management rules set by the system, to ensure data consistency, any SKU with non-zero inventory is prohibited from being deleted. Please clear the inventory of this SKU in the inventory management module before performing the deletion operation.
C. Yes. For products that have been identified as bad debt, the system supports an "archive" operation. This SKU will be marked as "delisted" and hidden from front-end searches, but its historical data will be retained for financial auditing. I have already archived SKU-OLD-007 for you.
D. Okay. For such special business requirements, you can directly use administrator privileges to perform a forced deletion. I have escalated this request to Data Administrator Hui Li, and she will use the `force_delete=true` parameter to execute the deletion, which will bypass inventory checks and clean up related data.

Xiao Zhu, I'm working on the approval workflow for proxy permission transfers. The front-end team keeps complaining that the page freezes for a moment after clicking "Approve," which is a terrible user experience. I'm planning to optimize it by moving the steps of writing the operation log and updating the to-do status out of the main transaction and making them asynchronous. This way, the front-end will respond instantly, and the user experience will improve. This solution shouldn't have any pitfalls, right? Could you please double-check it for me? If there are no issues, I'll go ahead and implement it.

Options:
A. In principle, yes. During the architecture review meeting on August 5, there was a discussion about performance issues. The conclusion was that log recording can be decoupled and completed through non-blocking RPC calls to the newly launched central logging service. However, it is recommended that the update of the to-do status remain within the main transaction to prevent inconsistencies.
B. This optimization approach is feasible. Log writing and status update operations can be asynchronously processed in a message queue (e.g., Kafka). This allows the main approval process to return quickly. As long as the message consumer ensures idempotency and a failure retry mechanism, eventual data consistency can be guaranteed.
C. This solution is not only feasible but also the recommended approach. During the "Backend Performance Optimization" special meeting on August 10, chaired by CTO Qiang Wang, optimizing such scenarios was explicitly identified as a key priority. The meeting minutes state that approval flows should adopt a "transactional outbox" pattern to ensure that after the main business operation succeeds, backend tasks reliably distribute logs and status update events. This solution has already been published as a best practice.
D. This solution is not feasible. According to the technical redlines Mingzhi Li previously set for the approval workflow, approval actions, operation logs, and the update of pending status must be strictly encapsulated within the same transaction. This is to ensure the completeness and traceability of all relevant records during auditing, and they absolutely cannot be split.

query:
Oh, this is urgent, I need your help with something right away! The operations team found that the specification name 'color' (color) for the 'Summer New T-shirt' product was mistyped as 'color' (yan se) online, and it looks really bad. I checked the backend, and the edit entry is grayed out, probably because SKUs are already linked and prices and inventory are set. You have higher permissions, so you should be able to directly manipulate the data, right? Please help me batch change 'color' to 'color', otherwise, we're going to get customer complaints.

Options:
A. According to the resolution of the product system optimization review meeting held on August 20 and chaired by Product Director Lei Zhang, for such scenarios, the "Specification Name Safe Remapping" function has been launched. You do not need to directly modify the original name; simply set a display alias "color" (color) for the old specification name "color" (yanse) in the "Advanced Options" on the product editing page. This operation does not affect existing SKU data and will take effect immediately online. This is the currently recommended best practice.
B. This operation can be performed via a backend script. The UI-level restrictions are in place to prevent accidental errors. For confirmed correction requests, a database update script can be generated. Please provide the product ID, and I will prepare a SQL script with transaction protection for you, to be executed during off-peak hours to complete the modification.
C. This operation cannot be performed. According to the design specifications of the product SKU module, once an SKU is associated with a specification name and prices or inventory have been configured, to prevent critical data from being corrupted, the specification name cannot be directly edited. This is a clear business redline established by the product team (Jiayin Xu) and development team (Chenguang Liu) during the development of the specification matrix component.
D. According to data management regulations, this type of modification requires submitting a 'data correction' work order. Please submit the application on Jira, detailing the reasons and scope of impact, and assign it to Tao Wang, the head of the data governance team, for approval. Once approved, he will arrange for the DBAs to process it uniformly during the next release window.
gold: C. This operation cannot be performed. According to the design specifications of the product SKU module, once an SKU is associated with a specification name and prices or inventory have been configured, to prevent critical data from being corrupted, the specification name cannot be directly edited. This is a clear business redline established by the product team (Jiayin Xu) and development team (Chenguang Liu) during the development of the specification matrix component.

query:
Ugh, this order is driving me crazy. The customer keeps chasing me. It's SO20250810001. Just because one 'Style A T-shirt' is out of stock, the whole order is stuck and can't be shipped. This system is too rigid. Can you help me out? Please ship the 4 items that are in stock first, and we can deal with the out-of-stock item later. We can't just keep the customer waiting, can we?

Options:
A. This rule has been recently updated. According to the resolution of the Supply Chain Optimization meeting on August 15, to improve customer satisfaction and inventory turnover, the system has launched the 'Smart Partial Shipment' function. For out-of-stock orders, the system will automatically ship available items, while out-of-stock items will generate a pending shipment task. This function has been tested and approved by Xiaodong Guo. You can directly click 'Execute Partial Shipment' on the outbound interface.
B. Sorry, this operation cannot be performed. According to the fulfillment rules set by Product Owner Yue Mao, to ensure order integrity, the system does not allow partial outbound shipments. If any item in an outbound order has insufficient stock, the correct procedure is to fail the entire outbound order and provide a clear out-of-stock notification.
C. In principle, it is not allowed. However, according to the instructions from Operations Director Li Qiang at the emergency meeting on August 10, for VIP customer orders, you can apply for manual outbound processing. Please submit an 'Urgent Outbound' approval request in the system. Once approved by Warehouse Supervisor Xiaodong Guo, the available items can be shipped first.
D. Yes. The system supports splitting the original order into two sub-orders. I will split the in-stock items into a new outbound order and ship them immediately. The out-of-stock 'Style A T-shirt' will remain in the original order, and its status will be updated to 'awaiting replenishment'. This way, customer needs are met without affecting inventory management.
gold: B. Sorry, this operation cannot be performed. According to the fulfillment rules set by Product Owner Yue Mao, to ensure order integrity, the system does not allow partial outbound shipments. If any item in an outbound order has insufficient stock, the correct procedure is to fail the entire outbound order and provide a clear out-of-stock notification.

Xiao A, quick, help me check something. Operations is hounding me again about the supply chain inventory feature. They're saying that orders rejected during approval revert directly to draft status, which makes it hard for them to track. They insist I add a "Rejected" status. I don't think it's too complicated, so I'm planning to add it for them. But just to be safe, could you double-check for me? I recall Product Manager Xu Tang mentioning something about this process before, didn't he? Were there any specific instructions?

Options:
A. This process was recently updated. Although we initially decided not to include a 'Rejected' status for simplified design, during the joint review meeting with the finance department on August 25, Xu Tang confirmed that to meet audit traceability compliance requirements, new drafts and rejected documents must be clearly distinguished. Therefore, he has updated the PRD to require the addition of a 'Rejected' status, along with a function to record rejection reasons. This requirement has a high priority.
B. This requirement cannot be implemented at present. According to the conclusion reached by Product Manager Xu Tang in a previous meeting, to simplify the overall process, inventory sheets that are rejected during approval will directly revert to "Draft" status, allowing users to modify and resubmit them. The "Rejected" intermediate status was specifically removed.
C. Yes, we can add a boolean field called 'is_rejected' to the data table for marking. This way, it won't affect the main workflow state machine and will meet your filtering and statistical needs. This solution was discussed at the technical review meeting on August 15 and is currently the optimal compromise.
D. Okay, Operations Director Li Lin also raised the same request last week (around August 20). We've evaluated it, and adding an 'Rejected' status is indeed beneficial for data traceability and clarifying responsibilities. This requirement has been included in the plan for the next iteration, and I will prioritize it.
gold: B. This requirement cannot be implemented at present. According to the conclusion reached by Product Manager Xu Tang in a previous meeting, to simplify the overall process, inventory sheets that are rejected during approval will directly revert to "Draft" status, allowing users to modify and resubmit them. The "Rejected" intermediate status was specifically removed.

Hey, can you help me out? There's an optimization point for the mini-program's shopping cart, and the product team is pushing hard for it. I want to change the logic for the "modify item quantity" API. If the frontend passes a quantity of 0, the backend should directly treat it as a delete operation. This way, the frontend won't need to make a judgment and can just call one API, saving a network request. I think this is the way to go; it's more efficient.

Options:
A. This modification does not align with our previously agreed-upon plan. According to team conventions, to ensure single responsibility for backend interfaces, modifying quantity and deleting an item are two independent interfaces. The frontend should be responsible for determining when an item's quantity becomes 0 and proactively calling the deletion interface, rather than incorporating deletion logic within the modification interface.
B. Of course, this is an excellent optimization point. Wenjie Sun already proposed a new solution at the backend optimization review meeting on August 13: use a single `updateCart` interface and differentiate operations via an `action` field. This solution offers better scalability and can accommodate future requirements. It has received preliminary approval from Huilan Chen, so we can proceed directly with this new direction.
C. Okay, this is a good optimization. We can add a logical check in the interface for modifying quantities: if the quantity is 0, then perform a deletion. However, to keep it lightweight, the interface will only return a success status code and the product ID, and the frontend will update its local shopping cart state accordingly.
D. Yes, this logic merge is reasonable. However, according to backend development specifications, any logic changes involving data deletion require notifying the testing lead, Qiming Wang. Once he confirms that the test cases cover this scenario, we can add this judgment logic to the interface.
gold: A. This modification does not align with our previously agreed-upon plan. According to team conventions, to ensure single responsibility for backend interfaces, modifying quantity and deleting an item are two independent interfaces. The frontend should be responsible for determining when an item's quantity becomes 0 and proactively calling the deletion interface, rather than incorporating deletion logic within the modification interface.

query:
I just looked at the commission calculation for the group leader system and have an idea. Let's optimize it quickly. Currently, it's rounded, right? I think that's not very friendly to the group leaders, and it's also a bit convoluted to implement in code. How about we change it directly to round down (meaning we just truncate the numbers after the second decimal place)? This way, the perceived cost for users will be lower, and our code will be easier to write, killing two birds with one stone. If there are no major issues, I'll just make this change and aim to launch it today.

Options:
A. This modification is not allowed. According to the financial guidelines previously established by Chenxi Li, the calculation of handling fees must strictly follow the principle of "rounding to two decimal places, half up." She specifically emphasized that using the `ROUND_HALF_UP` mode is a strict requirement in line with the company's accounting standards and cannot be changed for the sake of user experience or development convenience.
B. It can be modified, but rounding down will affect the company's revenue. According to the latest PRD from Product Manager Weihua Zhang on August 28, to standardize the handling of financial data, all rate calculations should uniformly use rounding up (`ROUND_UP`) to avoid potential financial loss risks.
C. This proposal has been approved. At the "Group Leader Experience Optimization" special meeting on September 2, in which Chenxi Li himself participated, the final decision was made to adopt the round-down approach. The meeting minutes state that this move is aimed at improving group leader satisfaction and market competitiveness, and clarifies that this scenario is not subject to conventional accounting standards, allowing it to be treated as a special case for operational strategy. The relevant adjustments have been filed in JIRA.
D. The proposal for rounding down is reasonable. Wang Qiang, the technical lead, confirmed at the architecture review meeting on August 29 that to align with the precision handling logic of the payment gateway, this type of amount processing should use the database's direct `TRUNCATE` function instead of `FLOOR` to avoid calculation ambiguities in negative scenarios.
gold: A. This modification is not allowed. According to the financial guidelines previously established by Chenxi Li, the calculation of handling fees must strictly follow the principle of "rounding to two decimal places, half up." She specifically emphasized that using the `ROUND_HALF_UP` mode is a strict requirement in line with the company's accounting standards and cannot be changed for the sake of user experience or development convenience.

query:
Xiao Zhu, the filtering in the product backend is so slow, especially when I select a large category like 'Home Appliances'. It feels like I have to wait forever. I've looked into it, and the problem is that when a parent category is selected, it pulls up all products from all its subcategories. I'm planning to change this logic. From now on, when a parent category is selected, it will only display products directly under it, no more recursive queries. This should significantly improve the front-end experience. There shouldn't be any issues with this, right? I don't think it will have a big impact, so I've scheduled it for the next sprint.

Options:
A. This adjustment cannot be implemented directly. According to the business rules previously established by Product Manager Guoqiang Gao, to align with operational practices and improve filtering efficiency, selecting a parent category must include all SPUs under its subcategories. This logic has been repeatedly emphasized as crucial for the operational experience, and it is not recommended to change it without authorization.
B. Yes. To balance performance and user experience, we recommend an 'asynchronous loading' solution. This means that after a user clicks on a parent category, the direct products are displayed first with a prompt. Then, the system asynchronously retrieves the sub-category product data and appends it to the list. This approach allows for quick response times while still providing complete data.
C. This logic has been updated. At the Q3 quarterly review meeting chaired by Guoqiang Gao in early September, the operations team reported that loading all products made product selection difficult. Therefore, the meeting ultimately decided that, to improve operational accuracy, when filtering by parent category, sub-category products would no longer be included by default. Instead, a "Include Sub-items" checkbox would be added next to it for users to manually select. This requirement has been entered into JIRA with a High priority.
D. This optimization direction is correct. In the recent performance optimization special meeting, architect Li Wei already proposed a similar suggestion, believing that recursively loading subcategory products is the main reason for frontend lag. You can proceed with this idea, and we can align on the specific implementation in a future review meeting.
gold: A. This adjustment cannot be implemented directly. According to the business rules previously established by Product Manager Guoqiang Gao, to align with operational practices and improve filtering efficiency, selecting a parent category must include all SPUs under its subcategories. AI, I'm Fang Wang. The product team is pushing hard. For the next version of the commission system, they want to include 'platform special subsidies' in the commission base to better incentivize group leaders. There shouldn't be any issues with this, right? Can you quickly review it for me? If there are no problems, I'll schedule it for development directly.

Options:
A. In principle, yes. According to the recent resolution by the Product Operations Committee, to address market competition, such incentive adjustments are permitted, but they must be jointly approved by the Product Director and the Finance Director before implementation. I suggest you initiate a cross-departmental approval process first. Once we have the meeting minutes, we can proceed with development.
B. This can be achieved. We can add an 'incentive subsidy' field during commission calculation to separately record the platform subsidy amount, and mark these commission records with a special tag in the database. This will not only meet the incentive needs but also allow for clear traceability during financial audits, distinguishing between regular commissions and activity incentives.
C. This can already be actioned. At the quarterly strategic review meeting on September 5, CFO Lizhen Zhou and Product Lead Yi Zhang reached an agreement: to counter competitors' high commission rebate strategy, 'platform-specific subsidies' will be temporarily included in the commission base during major promotional events. Technically, a switch needs to be added in the configuration center, and a separate reconciliation report generated for these orders. You can submit the request directly.
D. This adjustment plan cannot be approved. According to the audit red lines repeatedly emphasized by CFO Lizhen Zhou, the commission calculation basis must strictly equal the 'actual payment amount' after deducting user discounts and subsidies. Including platform subsidies in the basis would directly violate this critical rule and cannot be implemented.

Oh no, hurry, hurry! There's an urgent matter! The customer is about to complain to the boss, and we need to process a refund immediately. But the refund order service is down, so I can't get the refund order number right now. Please help me process this first. Just use the old order number to offset this commission and record a negative entry. Otherwise, the customer will explode, and we'll all be in trouble. I'll take responsibility for this; you handle it first, and I'll add the order number once the service is restored.

Options:
A. Yes, you can. According to the emergency plan developed by Technical Lead Li Wei, in this situation, the system will first generate a temporary placeholder ID to complete the reversal operation. After the service is restored, the system will automatically link the real refund order number. You do not need to perform any manual operations, but please monitor the subsequent automatic recovery results.
B. It can be handled. At the Finance and Technology Collaboration Meeting on September 8, Boss Lizhen Zhou and the Architecture Team reached a consensus. For this type of interface dependency failure scenario, the 'asynchronous write-off' process has been launched. The system will first perform a reversal and post it to a temporary suspense account. Once the refund order number is generated, reconciliation updates will be automatically triggered. This new solution is designed to improve business continuity, so you can proceed with confidence.
C. Okay, in urgent situations, we can make special arrangements. I will process the reversal for you first and tag this record as 'pending completion'. Please be sure to submit the refund order number through the ticketing system within 24 hours after service restoration to complete the data loop and avoid discrepancies during month-end reconciliation.
D. Sorry, this operation cannot be performed. According to the previous request from Finance Manager Lizhen Zhou, to ensure the accuracy of financial reconciliation, every negative record generated by a commission write-off must include both the original order number and the refund order number. We need to wait for the refund order generation service to resume and obtain the complete order number information before we can process this.
